rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so there is no evidence to exploit. The most informative first experiment is to establish a minimal baseline: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 (config_001). This configuration has the fewest design decisions (no aggregation, no fusion, no image encoder), making it a clean reference point. It tests the fundamental question: how well does a simple PCA-reduced RNA representation perform on this task? From this baseline, subsequent experiments can isolate the marginal contribution of each added complexity—multiprofile/aggregation (config_002/003), alternative RNA encoders (config_004/007), image modality (config_010), and multimodal fusion (config_016/017). Starting with the simplest configuration avoids conflating multiple design choices and ensures that any later performance gains can be attributed to specific additions rather than to an unknown interaction of several untested components simultaneously.

We have only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → acc 0.485), giving us essentially no information about whether the image modality contributes predictive signal or whether multimodal fusion is beneficial. The central question for this multimodal cellular profiling study is whether combining image with RNA improves over RNA alone. config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) is the minimal, clean extension of config_001: it keeps the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000), the same profile setting (singleprofile), and adds only the image modality with a standard ResNet50 and simple concat fusion. This isolates the effect of adding the image modality. If config_016 substantially outperforms 0.485, it justifies investing further in multimodal configurations and image encoder/aggregation choices; if it does not, it redirects the search toward RNA-only improvements (better encoders, multiprofile aggregation). This is the highest-information-gain experiment given the near-total absence of evidence about the image modality's contribution.

We have only two data points: RNA-only (pca_n2000, singleprofile) at 0.485 acc and multimodal (pca_n2000 + resnet50, concat, singleprofile) at 0.527 acc. The ~4% gain from adding the image is meaningful, but we cannot yet determine whether this gain reflects genuine complementary information from fusion or simply that the image features are a stronger predictor on their own. Testing config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) establishes the image-only baseline, directly isolating the image modality's independent contribution. This is the single most informative missing piece: if image-only is near 0.52, the multimodal gain is modest and fusion strategy matters less; if image-only is well below 0.48, the multimodal model is extracting real complementary signal and fusion/aggregation choices become high-value next questions. Under a tight budget with sparse evidence, reducing uncertainty about this fundamental modality-contribution question is more valuable than prematurely optimizing fusion type or profile setting, which would be harder to interpret without the image baseline.

Evidence: config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) achieves 0.485 acc, and config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, concat) improves to 0.527, confirming that adding image helps. However, the multiprofile axis (with aggregation) remains entirely untested. Question: Does using multiple profiles with avgpool aggregation improve over the single-profile baseline for the same RNA encoder (pca_n2000)? This directly compares to config_001, changing only the profile/aggregation setting while holding model setting and RNA encoder fixed. Why this is the best next experiment: The multiprofile decision is the most consequential unexplored axis—if it provides a meaningful gain in the simpler rna_only setting, it is very likely to compound in multimodal configurations (configs 018–051), and we should prioritize those; if it does not help, we can safely focus remaining budget on singleprofile configurations and other axes (RNA encoder, image encoder, fusion). Testing this in rna_only isolates the aggregation effect without the confound of multimodal fusion, making the result maximally interpretable under the limited budget.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, avgpool) is the best result so far at 0.591 acc, showing multiprofile aggregation is a major gain over singleprofile (0.485). Config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, concat) showed that adding resnet50 image features to RNA provides a modest but consistent boost (+0.042 over config_001). Uncertainty: it is unclear whether the image modality's benefit transfers to the multiprofile setting, or whether the stronger RNA signal in multiprofile makes the weak image contribution redundant. Config_018 tests exactly this: it keeps the proven multiprofile+avgpool+pca_n2000 backbone from config_002 and adds resnet50 with concat fusion (the same fusion that worked in config_016), changing only the modality composition. This is the most informative next step because (a) it directly extends the two strongest findings, (b) it isolates the effect of adding image to the multiprofile context, and (c) the result will clarify whether further multimodal experiments (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, ViT) are worth pursuing or whether the multiprofile RNA signal is already near its ceiling.

Evidence: config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is the best result so far at 0.619 acc / 0.610 F1, and multiprofile + avgpool was the single largest improvement observed (config_001→002: +0.106 RNA-only; config_016→018: +0.092 multimodal). However, we have zero information on whether transformer aggregation could further improve profile integration. Question: config_020 is identical to config_018 except aggregation changes from avgpool to transformer, giving a clean single-variable A/B test of the aggregation mechanism in the strongest known setting. Why this is the best next experiment: it directly exploits our strongest evidence with the minimal change needed to resolve whether the current avgpool is near-optimal or whether a sequence-aware aggregator captures inter-profile interactions that matter for the dominant RNA signal. The result immediately informs whether all future multiprofile configurations should default to transformer or avgpool, reducing uncertainty across the entire remaining search space.

Evidence: Our best result is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, concat) at 0.619 acc / 0.610 F1. All completed experiments use concat fusion; we have zero data on weighted fusion. The key uncertainty is whether the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted) meaningfully affects how the RNA and image signals combine, which is a fundamental architectural choice. Question: config_019 is identical to config_018 except fusion changes from concat to weighted, giving a clean single-variable A/B test that isolates the fusion effect. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) Fusion is a completely untested design axis, so any result reduces uncertainty on a core decision. (2) The answer generalizes across all future multimodal configurations—if weighted fusion helps, we adopt it everywhere; if not, we confirm concat suffices and can pivot to RNA encoder or image encoder exploration. (3) It is the most budget-efficient choice: one experiment resolves a binary architectural question with no confounds, rather than testing a new RNA encoder (e.g., scvi) which, while also informative, is a second-order question relative to how the two modalities are combined.

Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant signal (rna_only 0.485 vs image_only 0.208), and our best result (config_019, acc 0.639) uses PCA as the RNA encoder. The RNA encoder is the most important unexplored design axis—we have zero evidence on whether a learned encoder (scvi_n200) could improve upon PCA. Question: Does replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 in the multimodal multiprofile pipeline (keeping resnet50, avgpool, weighted fusion fixed) improve performance? This is a single-variable change from our current best (config_019), cleanly isolating the RNA encoder effect in the setting most likely to yield the highest accuracy. Why this is the best next experiment: It directly tests the highest-impact unexplored axis in the configuration regime where we expect the best results, and the outcome (improvement or not) will guide all subsequent encoder choices across the remaining search space.

The current best (config_031: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, acc=0.678) establishes a clear winning direction. However, the image encoder dimension is completely unexplored—only resnet50 has been tested. Config_037 changes exactly one variable (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while holding all other settings at their proven-best values (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted). This cleanly isolates the image encoder effect: if accuracy improves, the image modality is a bottleneck and a stronger visual representation unlocks further gains; if it does not, resnet50 is sufficient and the image contribution has plateaued. This is the highest-value single-variable test because it extends the current best along an untested axis, maintains the exploitation of the strong scvi+weighted+avgpool evidence, and directly informs whether further investment in the image branch is warranted under the limited budget.

The current best (config_037, acc=0.706) uses scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, but scgpt has never been tested in any experiment. The progression from pca→scvi yielded a meaningful +0.039 gain (config_019→config_031), and the image encoder upgrade (resnet50→ViT-L) added another +0.028 (config_031→config_037). The RNA encoder is the single most impactful design axis, and we have only tested 2 of 3 options. Config_049 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is a clean single-variable swap from config_037, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder in the best overall setting. If scgpt matches or beats scvi_n200, it opens a new optimization direction; if it underperforms, we confirm scvi_n200 as the preferred encoder and can focus remaining budget on finer-tuning (e.g., aggregation or fusion). This is the highest-information experiment because it resolves the largest remaining uncertainty in the design space with a direct A/B comparison against the current best.
